name: Old Gold Chocolate
funFactCorrect: Sir Macpherson Robertson created many classic chocolates after the gold rush ended, including Old Gold Chocolate, Cherry Ripe, and Freddo Frogs.
funFactIncorrect: While the creator of Old Gold Chocolate was born in Ballarat during the gold rush, the chocolate itself was not produced until 1916.

name: Thylacine Skull
funFactCorrect: This skull belongs to a Thylacine, also known as the Tasmanian Tiger, which were officially declared extinct in 1986.
funFactIncorrect: This skull belongs to a Thylacine, and while some were still living in Tasmania during the gold rush, they didn't have a big role in it.

name: Gregorian Astronomical Reflector Telescope
funFactCorrect: This type of telescope was invented in the 1600s by James Gregory, and makes things appear larger by reflecting light off two metal mirrors.
funFactIncorrect: This is a Gregorian reflector astronomical telescope which was invented in 1661, long before the Australian gold rush.

name: Trilobite
funFactCorrect: This is a fossilised Trilobite, which is a group of prehistoric animals with over 20,000 different species that have been found all over the world.
funFactIncorrect: This is a fossilised Trilobite, which is a type of animal that lived between 521 million years ago and 251 million years ago.

name: Monopoly
funFactCorrect: The first version of Monopoly was called “The Landlord's Game” and included two sets of rules - one known as Monopoly, and the other known as Prosperity.
funFactIncorrect: The first version of Monopoly was called “The Landlord's Game”, and was created by Lizzie Magie in 1903.

name: AWA Radiola Deep Image Television
funFactCorrect: Television did not begin regular broadcasting in Australia until 1956, and this particular AWA Radiola Deep Image Television was made in 1958.
funFactIncorrect: While this AWA Radiola television was made by an Australian company it wasn't produced until 1958, so most gold rush miners would not have lived to see it.

name: Mining Safety Lamp
funFactCorrect: These safety lamps were designed to prevent explosions in coal mines, and this particular type of lamp was used at Cooranbong Colliery in the 1990s.
funFactIncorrect: While this safety lamp may look like something a gold rush miner would carry, it was designed to be used in enclosed coal mines, not the open goldfields.

name: Miner's Helmet
funFactCorrect: This miner's helmet was manufactured by Protector Safety in 1989, and includes fittings for an electric cap lamp and battery cable.
funFactIncorrect: This miner's safety helmet would have looked out of place on the goldfields, where the main form of head protection was cloth hats.

name: Box Camera
funFactCorrect: This is an Austral No 1A Film & Plate camera, which was sold by Baker & Rouse Pty Ltd in the early 1900s.
funFactIncorrect: While photography was around during the gold rush, this particular type of box camera wasn't sold until the early 1900s.

name: Modern Backpack
funFactCorrect: This is a modern backpack, with features like padded shoulder straps and zippers which were not invented until after the gold rush.
funFactIncorrect: While prospectors may have found this modern backpack useful, they would have carried their belongings in swags or other types of luggage from that time.
